$0: Step pulse duration in microseconds — how long each step pulse is held high. Most drivers want a few microseconds; too short and the driver misses steps.
$1: Step idle delay in milliseconds before the steppers are allowed to disable after motion stops. 255 keeps the motors energised continuously (holding torque, but more heat).
$2: Step pulse invert mask (per-axis bitfield): inverts the step signal polarity for axes whose bit is set, to match a driver that expects active-low step pulses.
$3: Step direction invert mask (per-axis bitfield): flips the direction signal for axes whose bit is set, so a positive command moves the axis the way you expect.
$4: Invert the stepper-enable signal. Set it if the drivers are enabled by a high level rather than grbl's default active-low enable.
$5: Invert limit-pin input mask (per-axis bitfield): treat a limit switch as triggered on the opposite level. Set it to match normally-open vs normally-closed switch wiring.
$6: Invert the probe-pin input, so a probe that closes (vs opens) on contact reads correctly. Pair it with $19 if the probe input also needs its pull-up disabled.
$10: Status-report options bitmask: selects which fields the `<…>` real-time report includes (machine position, buffer state, etc.). The sender parses whatever the firmware chooses to emit.
$11: Junction deviation in mm — the cornering aggressiveness the planner uses to decide how fast it may round a corner without stopping. Larger is faster but rounds corners more.
$12: Arc tolerance in mm — the maximum chord error when G2/G3 arcs are flattened into line segments. Smaller is smoother but produces more segments.
$13: Report positions in inches instead of millimetres. A display preference only; it does not change how G-code is interpreted.
$19: Disable the internal pull-up on the probe pin (Galdr/grblHAL). Set it when the probe circuit supplies its own pull-up or pull-down and the internal one would fight it.
$20: Enable soft limits: refuse any move that would exceed the axis max-travel ($130…). Requires homing ($22) to be enabled first, since the limits are measured from the homed origin.
$21: Enable hard limits: an asserted limit switch during motion triggers an immediate alarm/stop. Protects the machine when a move would otherwise crash into an end-stop.
$22: Enable the homing cycle ($H). Required before soft limits ($20) can be turned on; many homing settings ($23–$27) only take effect once this is enabled. Applies on the next reset.
$23: Homing direction invert mask (per-axis bitfield): chooses which way each axis seeks its limit switch during homing. Set it so each axis homes toward its switch, not away from it.
$24: Homing locate feed rate (mm/min): the slow second approach used to precisely find the switch after the fast seek. Slower is more repeatable.
$25: Homing search seek rate (mm/min): the fast initial approach toward the limit switch during homing, before the slow locate pass ($24).
$26: Homing switch debounce delay in milliseconds — how long a switch reading must stay stable to count as a real trigger, rejecting electrical bounce.
$27: Homing pull-off distance in mm — how far each axis backs off its limit switch after homing, so the switch is released and hard limits ($21) do not immediately re-trigger.
$30: Maximum spindle speed in RPM — the speed that maps to full spindle output (100% PWM / 10 V). S-words are scaled between $31 and this value.
$31: Minimum spindle speed in RPM — the speed that maps to the lowest non-zero spindle output. S-words below this are clamped up to it.
$32: Laser mode: in laser mode the spindle output tracks feed rate dynamically and does not pause for speed changes. Leave it off for a rotary milling spindle.
$100: Distance the X axis travels per step, in steps/mm. Derived from motor steps/rev, microstepping, and the mechanical reduction; the basis of all positioning accuracy.
$101: Distance the Y axis travels per step, in steps/mm. Derived from motor steps/rev, microstepping, and the mechanical reduction; the basis of all positioning accuracy.
$102: Distance the Z axis travels per step, in steps/mm. Derived from motor steps/rev, microstepping, and the mechanical reduction; the basis of all positioning accuracy.
$103: Rotation the rotary A axis travels per step, in steps/deg. Derived from motor steps/rev, microstepping, and the mechanical reduction; the basis of all rotary positioning accuracy.
$110: Maximum feed rate for the X axis (mm/min) — the ceiling rapids and feeds are clamped to. Set it to the fastest reliable speed the axis can sustain without stalling.
$111: Maximum feed rate for the Y axis (mm/min) — the ceiling rapids and feeds are clamped to. Set it to the fastest reliable speed the axis can sustain without stalling.
$112: Maximum feed rate for the Z axis (mm/min) — the ceiling rapids and feeds are clamped to. Set it to the fastest reliable speed the axis can sustain without stalling.
$113: Maximum feed rate for the rotary A axis (deg/min) — the ceiling rapids and feeds are clamped to. Set it to the fastest reliable speed the axis can sustain without stalling.
$120: Maximum acceleration for the X axis (mm/s²). Higher values cut cycle time but risk skipped steps; the planner uses it to ramp speed in and out of every move.
$121: Maximum acceleration for the Y axis (mm/s²). Higher values cut cycle time but risk skipped steps; the planner uses it to ramp speed in and out of every move.
$122: Maximum acceleration for the Z axis (mm/s²). Higher values cut cycle time but risk skipped steps; the planner uses it to ramp speed in and out of every move.
$123: Maximum acceleration for the rotary A axis (deg/s²). Higher values cut cycle time but risk skipped steps; the planner uses it to ramp speed in and out of every move.
$130: Maximum travel for the X axis (mm), measured from the homed origin. Soft limits ($20) use this to refuse moves that would run past the axis envelope.
$131: Maximum travel for the Y axis (mm), measured from the homed origin. Soft limits ($20) use this to refuse moves that would run past the axis envelope.
$132: Maximum travel for the Z axis (mm), measured from the homed origin. Soft limits ($20) use this to refuse moves that would run past the axis envelope.
$133: Maximum travel for the rotary A axis (deg), measured from the homed origin. Soft limits ($20) use this to refuse moves that would run past the axis envelope.
$140: Motor RMS run current for the X axis (mA), programmed into the TMC2209 driver. Set it to the stepper's rated current; too high overheats the motor, too low loses torque and skips steps.
$141: Motor RMS run current for the Y axis (mA), programmed into the TMC2209 driver. Set it to the stepper's rated current; too high overheats the motor, too low loses torque and skips steps.
$142: Motor RMS run current for the Z axis (mA), programmed into the TMC2209 driver. Set it to the stepper's rated current; too high overheats the motor, too low loses torque and skips steps.
$143: Motor RMS run current for the rotary A axis (mA), programmed into the TMC2209 driver. Set it to the stepper's rated current; too high overheats the motor, too low loses torque and skips steps.
$150: Microstepping divisor for the X axis (a power of two, e.g. 16). Higher microstepping is smoother and quieter but coarser in torque; it must agree with the steps/mm ($100) calibration.
$151: Microstepping divisor for the Y axis (a power of two, e.g. 16). Higher microstepping is smoother and quieter but coarser in torque; it must agree with the steps/mm ($101) calibration.
$152: Microstepping divisor for the Z axis (a power of two, e.g. 16). Higher microstepping is smoother and quieter but coarser in torque; it must agree with the steps/mm ($102) calibration.
$153: Microstepping divisor for the rotary A axis (a power of two, e.g. 16). Higher microstepping is smoother and quieter but coarser in torque; it must agree with the steps/deg ($103) calibration.
$376: Rotary-axes bitmask (Galdr DOC-10): marks which axes are angular (degrees, continuous rollover) rather than linear. On this machine only bit 3 (the A axis) is meaningful — $376=8 makes A rotary, $376=0 treats A as a 4th linear axis.
$392: Spindle spin-up delay in seconds (Galdr DOC-07): after M3/M4 the planner inserts a synchronised dwell of this long so the spindle reaches speed before the first cut. 0 disables the delay.
$393: Spindle reverse dwell in seconds (Galdr DOC-07): the spin-down pause forced on an M3↔M4 direction reversal — the spindle is stopped and allowed to settle before reversing, protecting the drive.
$481: Auto status-report interval in milliseconds (grblHAL $481): when non-zero the firmware pushes a `<…>` report on this cadence without the sender polling `?`. 0 disables it; valid non-zero values are 100–1000 ms.
